_comment: Executable phase contract for project-genesis-chain. Required planning phases without reliable local specialist skills are agent-handled instead of routed to unavailable dependencies.
description: Greenfield project creation from intake to release-ready local repository with explicit approval gates and evidence-based validation.

phases.name: Step 0 - Capture project intake and execution mode
phases.reason: Capture the minimum reliable context before creating artifacts or source files.
phases.query_suffix: Create a concise intake brief with project name, target path, product goal, primary users, non-goals, stack preferences, constraints, MVP boundary, execution mode, approval boundaries, and open questions. Do not create source files yet.

phases.name: Step 1 - Establish project-local memory and constitution
phases.reason: Define stable project principles, memory boundaries, assumptions, quality bar, release discipline, and skill-routing expectations.
phases.query_suffix: Create the project constitution and assumptions ledger. Use .agentspec/memory/constitution.md and .agentspec/memory/assumptions.md when persistence is approved. Keep shared-memory concerns out of this project unless the user explicitly asks for cross-project reuse.

phases.name: Step 2 - Draft product specification
phases.reason: Turn the intake brief and constitution into a reviewable product spec before backlog or architecture work.
phases.query_suffix: Produce specs/001-initial-product/product-spec.md with problem, users, goals, non-goals, functional scope, non-functional requirements, assumptions, constraints, risks, and explicit out-of-scope items.

phases.name: Step 3a - Generate epics and user stories
phases.reason: Convert the product spec into structured epics, stories, and traceability-ready backlog artifacts.

phases.name: Step 3b - Draft testable acceptance criteria
phases.reason: Create behavior-level acceptance criteria before implementation and test planning.

phases.name: Step 4 - Review requirements for testability and ambiguity
phases.reason: Find ambiguity, missing non-functional requirements, and risky assumptions before architecture decisions become expensive.
phases._hitl_note: Gate before architecture. The human should answer blocking questions or approve proceeding with documented assumptions.

phases.name: Step 5 - Create architecture plan
phases.reason: Define architecture, stack decisions, boundaries, data model, API shape, UI architecture, deployment assumptions, and validation strategy.
phases.query_suffix: Produce specs/001-initial-product/architecture.md. Include context, constraints, selected stack, alternatives considered, module boundaries, data model, API/service boundaries, UI architecture, security/privacy posture, deployment assumptions, observability, validation strategy, and decision records.

phases.name: Step 6 - Create implementation task plan
phases.reason: Convert approved specification and architecture into ordered implementation tasks with validation commands and traceability.
phases._hitl_note: Gate before repository bootstrap and implementation. The human approves target path, stack, install/network actions, and the first vertical slice.
phases.query_suffix: Produce specs/001-initial-product/tasks.md and traceability notes. Tasks must be ordered, scoped, testable, and mapped to acceptance criteria. Call out dependencies, file targets when knowable, validation commands, and approval-sensitive actions.

phases.name: Step 7 - Bootstrap repository skeleton
phases.reason: Create the approved repository structure and starter files using the selected stack and local conventions.
phases.query_suffix: Bootstrap only inside the approved target path through project-bootstrapper-skill. Let that skill select stack-specific creation skills, conservative fallback scaffolds, or native tooling when available and approved. Do not install dependencies, initialize Git, or download templates unless approval and environment permissions allow it. Record every generated file and any skipped setup.

phases.name: Step 8 - Implement first vertical slice
phases.reason: Implement the smallest independently demonstrable slice using the approved repository, tasks, and acceptance criteria.
phases.query_suffix: Treat this as the first approved feature in a newly bootstrapped repository. Implement only the first independently demonstrable vertical slice. Keep source, tests, docs, and traceability aligned. If no repository was bootstrapped or approved, mark this phase blocked.

phases.name: Step 9a - Unit and component validation
phases.reason: Run or add repository-native unit and component tests for the implemented slice.
phases.query_suffix: If the repository has no executable source or no suitable unit/component surface yet, state exactly: 'unit validation: not applicable for this slice' and stop.

phases.name: Step 9b - API and service contract validation
phases.reason: Validate API contracts and service behavior when the slice exposes REST, HTTP, event, or service boundaries.
phases.query_suffix: If the bootstrapped project has no API or service boundary yet, state exactly: 'api contract validation: not applicable for this slice' and stop.

phases.name: Step 9c - Browser or end-to-end validation
phases.reason: Validate user-facing browser flows when the project has a UI.
phases.query_suffix: If the bootstrapped project has no browser UI yet, state exactly: 'e2e validation: not applicable for this slice' and stop.

phases.name: Step 9d - Responsive validation
phases.reason: Validate responsive behavior for UI surfaces across a practical viewport matrix.
phases.query_suffix: If the project has no responsive UI surface yet, state exactly: 'responsive validation: not applicable for this slice' and stop.

phases.name: Step 9e - Accessibility validation
phases.reason: Audit accessibility for UI surfaces introduced by the first slice.
phases.query_suffix: If the project has no user-facing UI yet, state exactly: 'accessibility validation: not applicable for this slice' and stop.

phases.name: Step 10 - Review validation evidence
phases.reason: Review validation evidence, coverage quality, gaps, and false-confidence risks.

phases.name: Step 11 - Audit release readiness
phases.reason: Run an audit-only hardening pass before declaring the project release-ready.
phases.query_suffix: Run audit mode only unless the human explicitly approves refactoring. Focus on first-slice code, generated architecture, dependency risk, security, testability, maintainability, and release blockers.

phases.name: Step 12 - Prepare local release artifacts
phases.reason: Prepare changelog, version plan, release notes, and readiness report without publishing.
phases.query_suffix: STOP BEFORE PUSHING TO GITHUB. Prepare local release artifacts, changelog entry, version plan, release notes, and readiness report. Do not push, tag, publish, deploy, or create a GitHub Release unless the human explicitly approves.

phases.name: Step 13 - Deliver project genesis summary
phases.reason: Summarize generated artifacts, code, verification evidence, risks, release readiness, and next decisions.
phases.query_suffix: Produce a concise final project genesis report with project summary, artifact paths, repository path, implemented slice, validation evidence, audit findings, release readiness, blocked items, and recommended next actions. Base every claim on prior phase evidence.
